title: "Get Started"
author: "S. Le Boulanger"

## Find your course

Open the navbar's Niveau menus and pick a year group (Klassenstufe). Each course
landing page introduces the year's recurring cast (the named
characters who reappear across Units), shows the twelve Units as a
card grid, and links to the schedule.

- **Track G+M (Kl. 5–10):** grundlegend + mittleres Niveau, two
  Niveaustufen taught alongside each other. Use the *G* variant for
  Hauptschul-bound students, *M* for intermediate secondary certificate (Realschulabschluss)-bound
  students. Many Units include both stimulus levels in one slide
  deck so a mixed classroom uses one source.
- **Track E (Kl. 5–13):** erweitertes Niveau through school-leaving examination (Abitur). From
  Klasse 11 onwards, Units are tagged either *E-BF* (Basisfach) or
  *E-LF* (Leistungsfach).

## Use a Unit in class

Every Unit follows the same five-step shape:

1. **Activate** — warm-up that surfaces prior knowledge.
2. **Input** — the target text, transcript, grammar focus, or worked
   example.
3. **Practise** — guided exercises with answer key.
4. **Produce** — open task: speaking prompt, writing, mediation.
5. **Reflect** — self-assessment against the Unit's Can-do
   objectives.

A typical session uses the slide deck (Reveal.js) for delivery and
the HTML article for follow-up reading. The slides include speaker
notes with timing estimates, transitions, and Niveau-aware
differentiation prompts.

## Use the four downloads per Unit

Every Unit's "Downloads" callout links to four artefacts:

- **Unit article (HTML)** — the page itself.
- **Slide deck (HTML)** — the Reveal.js companion.
- **Worksheet (PDF)** — student handout. Placeholder for now;
  the canonical filename is fixed so real worksheets drop in
  without site-code changes.
- **Exam example (PDF)** — Klassenarbeit (Kl. 5–10) or school-leaving examination (Abitur) task
  (Kl. 11–13) with answer key and rubric, attributed and
  watermarked.

Article and slides are live web pages; worksheet and exam are PDFs
for offline use and copying.

## Plan a unit cycle

Each Unit is sized for ~3 weeks (so 12 Units fill ~36 teaching weeks
of a BW school year). The class test (Klassenarbeit) at the end is the assessment
event. For Track E Kl. 11–13, the school-leaving examination (Abitur)-format task at the end of
each Unit can be used either as a Klausur or as a low-stakes
practice run before the actual school-leaving examination (Abitur).

## Adapt for your school

Materials are CC-BY-SA 4.0 — fork the repo, adapt the YAML curriculum
outline, and re-render. The `_resources/` folder holds the structured
Bildungsplan map; everything else flows from there.
